items.title: Water bottles
items.body: We drink a lot of water in PreK and we love the earth. Please send a filled reusable water bottle each day, labeled with your child's name. Our classrooms have a filling station, and we use the bottles at snack and lunch.

items.title: Velcro shoes
items.body: Growing self-help skills is a big part of the PreK year. Please send your child in Velcro shoes they can manage themselves. We're on the playground daily and in P.E., so choose athletic footwear that moves easily and safely.

items.title: Under wraps
items.body: On Orientation Day you'll find our classrooms all wrapped up. Over the first few days, children discover the materials in a guided way — it builds excitement about our supplies while we teach constructive use, cooperation, and care for our space.

items.title: A comfort item
items.body: Sometimes you just need a cozy blanket or stuffed animal nearby. If that helps your child settle in, send it in the school tote bag. It lives in the bag during the day, and they can visit it during free play.

items.title: Tote bags and lunch boxes
items.body: PreK provides a Harding tote bag — they work much better at this age. If you've already bought a backpack, save it for kindergarten. We eat lunch in our classrooms on full days, so please send a lunch with reusable utensils and a water bottle.

items.title: How it works
items.body: A digital monthly snack calendar goes out with sign-ups for Mondays and Fridays. On Tuesday, Wednesday, and Thursday teachers provide Harding-supplied snacks, with a special focus on grains on Wednesdays. Signing up is completely voluntary — and hopefully fun.

items.title: Moo Mondays
items.body: Hard cheese, bulk yogurt (no tubes or individually packaged cups), hard-boiled eggs, cottage cheese, coconut-milk yogurt, kefir, pimento cheese.

items.title: Fruit Fridays
items.body: Whole fresh fruit — bunches of bananas, a box of clementines, small apples.

items.title: Why bulk
items.body: We're glad to cut up a large block of cheese or scoop out yogurt servings. It eliminates individual packaging and meets our goal of reducing the waste we produce.

items.title: Food allergies
items.body: If there are allergies in the classroom we'll share those details before the snack curriculum begins, and let you know which foods to avoid to keep everyone safe.

items.title: Sustainable rooms
items.body: We recycle, reuse, and reduce wherever we can — fabric napkins and reusable water bottles at snack and lunch.

items.title: Green art — send it in!
items.body: We love recycled materials in our Free Art Center and structured projects. Interesting cardboard, old game or puzzle pieces, baby food jars, cast-off jewelry, newspaper, paper towel rolls — just about anything. When in doubt, send it in. We'll use it.

items.title: We go outside in all weather
items.body: The NOP is a large part of the PreK curriculum, which means we often learn outside. We observe nature, build with natural materials, cooperate, and practice risk-taking. Rain boots and a hooded rain jacket stay in the classroom all year so we can stay dry every day.

items.title: Getting to know each other
items.body: We spend the first six weeks getting to know one another as unique individuals, as members of a family, and as a classroom community.

items.title: Building the community
items.body: Daily Morning Meetings and fun activities. This month we'll complete a "Who Am I?" photo project, a self-portrait in paint, and a family drawing.

items.title: Rules and routines
items.body: Together we create our classroom rules and play plenty of name-learning games, learn new routines, and start exploring the Harding campus.

items.title: Toward the end of the month
items.body: We introduce the Estimation Jar, Heggerty phonemic awareness activities, Everyday Math, and Handwriting Without Tears.

blocks.text: Dear Pre-K Families,

What a wonderful week we had celebrating the joys of fall, all while outside! The weather was beautiful, and your children embraced every moment of learning and playing in the NOP.  Here’s a look back at our outdoor autumn week together:
Art in Nature Children painted watercolor pumpkins with tree stumps as their stools and tabletops.
Dining Al Fresco Each day, everyone enjoyed snacks and lunch picnic-style in the shade. It was a fun way to connect with one another in a different setting.
Spanish Al Aire Libre Spanish class also went outside! The children practiced their counting and went on a color hunt.
Outdoor Exploration

The children collaborated to move large tree limbs and build imaginative new structures. They also explored flowering gourd vines, closely observed a variety of insects, ran a salon, started a band, and took care of pumpkin “babies”. This open ended play allowed your child to embrace their imagination while developing their interpersonal, social-emotional, and problem solving skills.
Seed Exploration

Students had a blast dissecting a pumpkin, scooping out the pulp, cleaning the seeds, and learning all about the pumpkin life cycle. They even got to taste roasted pumpkin seeds during snack time! Based on the story Pumpkin Jack, we kicked off our own 'Pumpkin Jack' experiment! Each class carved a pumpkin and placed it in a jar with soil, giving us a front-row seat to watch the decomposition process. We're excited to observe the full life cycle, with the goal of planting the vines in the spring to grow our very own pumpkins. You can learn more about the experiment [here](https://www.simplykinder.com/pumpkin-jack-in-the-classroom/).
Eighth grade buddies joined us again, this time working alongside their Pre-K friends to dissect and count the seeds in a cherry tomato.

Storytime in the Shade The librarian, Mrs. Montgomery, joined us in the NOP to read a variety of books about dogs, including Some Dogs [Do](https://www.publishersweekly.com/9780763622015), Harry the Dirty [Dog](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=vMiGX0OSiyM), and Bark, [George!](https://www.amazon.com/Bark-George-Jules-Feiffer/dp/0062051857) It was the perfect way to enjoy literature amongst nature.
Dancing in the Sunshine
The children had a blast in dance class dancing in the open air and expressing themselves through movement and rhythm.
Science in the Fall Breeze Ms. Perkins joined us outside for Science this week. She read Spookly, The Square Pumpkin and then we explored shapes with chalk.
It was a memorable week full of fresh air, friendship, and fall magic. We loved every minute,  and your children did too!

Happy Weekend!
Lauren and Greg
Good Afternoon Pre-K Families,

This week we expanded upon our study of maps into the shapes we see around us in the world.  We traced objects from our classroom aerial mapping project and discussed our observations. Students then practiced tracing these shapes by squeezing glue bottles, adding a fun multi-dimensional texture to their map.

As we moved around campus, the children participated in shape walks to spot geometry in our everyday environment. They discovered plenty of circles, squares, rectangles, and triangles, as well as a hexagon, an octagon, and a rhombus! In the classroom students enjoyed making playdoh shapes and proudly identified the number of corners and sides.

We also launched our unit on owls! We began by gathering what the students already know about owls, which we will revisit at the end of the unit to reflect on everything they have learned. To celebrate the launch, we created a cooperative owl artwork. Working together with recycled paper scraps and feathers, the children layered materials onto the owl's body and wings. They had a wonderful time watching their collective creation come to life! Last, but not least, students had to agree on a name for their owl. This took a lot of patience, collaboration, and even some voting to finally agree on a name.

In lieu of assembly, we met our 8th grade buddies! The 8th graders lined the hallway holding photos of their Pre-K buddy, and our students walked down the hall to find their picture and greet their new friend. Afterward, we gathered in the classrooms to share a snack and spend time getting to know each other.

We had another special guest visit Pre K this week! Norman the therapy dog stopped by our classrooms, giving students a wonderful opportunity to practice kindness and gentle interaction with a furry friend. Highlights included watching Norman perform his favorite trick, carrying three tennis balls at once, and getting to shower him with soft pets. You can learn more about Norman and his book [here](https://normanatyourservice.com/).

Finally, a heartfelt thank you to all the families who provided snacks and helped wash napkins these past few weeks. Your support means so much to us, and the children have thoroughly enjoyed trying new foods and learning about where they come from and how they are made. Lauren and Greg
Good Afternoon Pre-K Families!

This week, our learning centered around the theme "Where We Live." We explored concepts of home and community, sharing ideas like how maps help us when we’re lost, that homes are strong and safe, and that we can use maps on phones to find fun places to go! Using repurposed wooden blocks, the children designed their own houses, drawing detailed doors and windows, before adding beautiful watercolor details. These special creations are heading to our block center, where they are sure to spark plenty of imaginative play.

We continued our map exploration by reading Rosie’s [Walk](https://www.simonandschuster.com/books/Rosies-Walk/Pat-Hutchins/Classic-Board-Books/9781481422758). As one teacher read the story aloud, the other drew a live map tracking the fox’s misadventures along the way. Afterwards, students brainstormed and developed maps that held personal meaning for them. We prompted them with a question: “What map can you make to share your interests?” Using the newly introduced medium of oil pastels, they brought their ideas to life by creating everything from imaginative treasure maps to detailed layouts of their own homes and bedrooms. To cap off our mapping unit, students worked collaboratively to create an aerial bird's-eye view of our classroom!

In science, we explored various seeds around campus. Ms. Perkins challenged everyone to open a stubborn sycamore seed, a process that took stomping, pressing, and ultimately a hammer to crack open!  Students then carefully used tweezers to pick through the fibers and reveal the seed hidden in the center.

At Tuesday's assembly, we celebrated Hispanic Heritage Month by learning about the eight Spanish-speaking countries that competed in the World Cup. Finally, on Friday we had the pleasure of welcoming Harding’s Artist in Residence, Mandy Rogers Horton, to our classroom for a hands-on art project.

Good Afternoon Pre-K Families!

What an incredible week of firsts! On Monday, we gathered with Kindergarten for our first full Primary Division Morning Meeting of the year. On Thursday, we took our very first Harding bus ride for a wonderful trip to the Frist Art Museum. To top it all off, on Friday we met this year’s Artist in Residence, Mandy Rogers Horton, who introduced us to the creative concept of "Mapping Time."

As part of our Responsive Classroom approach, our Pre-K class gathered to brainstorm and create our classroom rules for the year, rooted directly in each student’s hopes and dreams. Once we agreed on our rules, every child added their fingerprint in a special ceremony, committing to a safe, fun, and supportive year of learning and growing together!

In the Discovery Lab with Ms. Perkins, your children became true engineers! They began by exploring aluminum foil through sight (shiny), sound (crunchy), and touch (bendy). Everyone wrapped foil around their finger to shape a merperson tail, leading into our engineering challenge: design a merperson tail that floats while balancing three beads on top. It was an amazing way to practice fine motor skills, problem-solving, and perseverance!

The letter of the week was E. Students brainstormed E-words and practiced writing it in their Handwriting Without Tears workbook. Children quickly noticed how similar E is to the letter F, what a great connection!

The "Me Box" begins on Tuesday! Each day, the box will travel home with a different student. Please guide your child in choosing 2–3 items that hold personal meaning to bring back the next day. A few great ideas include a favorite seashell from a trip, a sports jersey, or a photo of a family pet. Your child will then have the opportunity to present their items to the class and share why those objects are special to them.

Good Afternoon Pre-K Families,

Thank you so much for joining us on Wednesday evening! It was a joy to spend time with you. We truly appreciate your participation, your curiosity, and especially your creativity during our paint mixing activity. The children were thrilled to read your notes and loved seeing their unique paint colors!

We had a wonderful and busy four-day week in Pre-K! Our theme this week was feelings, and we explored much more than just happy and sad. The children identified and expressed a wide range of emotions, including feeling relaxed, worried, and loved. We took expressive "feelings photos," which will be displayed in our classroom. It was such a joy to see your children share their emotions through these photos. One of the books we read, How Are You [Peeling?](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=GsLR1lfeVfM), helped us explore feelings in a playful and creative way, using expressive fruits and vegetables.
Our letter of the week was F. We practiced building the letter, learned the sound it makes, and worked on writing it in our Handwriting Without Tears workbook.

We also spent time learning about families and celebrating how every family is unique. Using the family photos you provided, the children drew their own family portraits and had the chance to share about the special people in their lives. We read Who Is In My [Family](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=FtWIOY_YUKA), which helped reinforce the idea that families come in all shapes and sizes.

As discussed at Back to School Night, PreK will launch our snack curriculum next week. This initiative serves as a hands-on extension of our health and nutrition curriculum, and social studies learning goals. Throughout the year, students will explore snack ideas designed to help them build a deeper connection to their food sources while learning practical ways to reduce waste.

blocks.text: Happy Weekend!
Lauren and Greg

This week in PreK, we continued our exploration of self-identity by celebrating what makes each of us special. The children created full-body tracings with the help of their teachers and painted them to reflect their unique and beautiful bodies. We read I Like [Myself!](https://www.amazon.com/I-Like-Myself-Karen-Beaumont/dp/0152020136/ref=sr_1_1?dib=eyJ2IjoiMSJ9.ufV5c9IEE_-WxpLCzw8CEtyX5BmDd88jWfZ_pEZk0X-rT9BPx8QdTonbqM_i0JY0Q0CTdhz9u60It6a4VGsWCJ1x7nD8PykHRIskuv9qlZ59TIKUSJA8vYdT1nhkVdLeriEojNYVmbNS0j9VsYveGW7uJqM3OM-fZ7GgNmYEm9L-7S9b_xx0Xsp8Pr8dwNOPjm7guaTepNrKDvhYnsxwekt6geJhpezuwNzweXQVEYY.ppi1nFcoZljbtv3z6MygsPNrZC6rCdMmHdt2-OnvIgE&dib_tag=se&keywords=I+Like+Myself+Book&qid=1756345726&sr=8-1) and had thoughtful discussions about what we appreciate about ourselves and each other.

Using handheld mirrors for reference, the children also drew and painted self-portraits with watercolors.  To aid in this process, students were introduced to Mat [Man](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zcGs7__1XFs), a fun and helpful tool for building body awareness.  It was truly a joy to see each child’s creativity and individuality shine through in their artwork!

Lions and lizards and Legos, oh my! This week we took a closer look at the letter L. The class built the letter L using wooden manipulatives and worked on writing L in their Handwriting Without Tears workbooks. We also introduced an exciting concept: all letters and numbers are made from a combination of four basic lines: big line, little line, big curve, and little curve.
At home, you can continue the fun by going on a letter L hunt around the house or neighborhood. See how many objects you and your child can find that start with the letter L!
This week, we traveled to Library with Mrs. Montgomery and read Earl the Squirrel, one of her favorite books. We also met Ms. Burnett, our Spanish teacher and enjoyed our first few Spanish classes.
We hope you have a wonderful long weekend! We'll see your children back on Tuesday for an exciting week all about the letter F, focusing on feelings, family, and found objects.
Happy Long Weekend!
Lauren and Greg

Whew! Your child made it through the first full week of school! This week was filled with getting to know one another, learning classroom routines, and meeting special area teachers. Students have also been introduced to new items in the classroom, including the painting easel, tangrams, and a variety of blocks.

Students continue to build their self-reliance skills as they practice their three step morning routine, take on helper jobs within the classroom, and work together to clean up after snack and lunch. To this end, if your child is bringing a sweater or sweatshirt to school, please work with them to practice independently putting it on, taking it off, and getting it right side out. Your child will be so proud to add another self-sufficient skill to their growing roster!

This week, we read Little Blue and Little Yellow by Leo Lionni. Through guided discovery, the children explored playdough, noticing how it feels, sounds, and smells, and thinking about what they can create with it. Each child started with a little blue ball of playdough and was then given a little ball of yellow. Some children immediately mixed the two colors together, while others mixed them a little at a time. Everyone was delighted to discover that mixing blue and yellow makes green! Students also explored playdough tools and experimented with the different ways they can be used.

Students watched and listened to the Secret Stories Better Alphabet song [LINKED](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=q3M_rdef7sw) here. This song will be revisited throughout the year as students delve deeper into letters and the sounds they make as an important pre-reading skill. Screen time in Pre-K is thoughtfully limited, with physical teaching tools and manipulatives used whenever possible. Occasionally, however, a short, intentionally chosen video can be a helpful way to introduce a concept or reinforce learning. One student even referred to the Smart Board as the “learning TV,” which honestly might need to become its official name!
Next week, students will begin the Handwriting Without Tears program, create self-portraits, and explore more of campus as they travel to the rest of their special area classes.
